name: Domaine Durieu Châteauneuf-du-Pape Cuvée Lucile Avril 2016
text:
## Domaine Durieu Châteauneuf-du-Pape Cuvée Lucile Avril 2016

**The story.** Domaine Durieu took its modern shape in the 1970s, with Paul Durieu as the family's driving force. The vineyard in its current form is young, but the land has been in the family a very long time: the Avril family, on Paul's mother's side, came to [Châteauneuf-du-Pape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape_AOC) in the 1500s, and some vines still in use were planted before the First World War. Today brothers Vincent and François run the estate, which uses no pesticides and is known also for its Côtes du Rhône and [Plan de Dieu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%B4tes_du_Rh%C3%B4ne_AOC) wines ([Bruno Lafon Selection, technical sheet](https://vincod.com/SQ8H1E/get/print)).

**The wine: Lucile Avril.** Named for Paul's mother, Lucile Avril is the estate's top red, from its oldest plots, including old [Grenache](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grenache), on the Farguerol plateau of rolled pebbles, the [galets roulés](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galets_roul%C3%A9s). The importer's sheet gives about 80% Grenache, 10% [Mourvèdre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mourv%C3%A8dre) and 10% [Syrah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrah), hand-harvested, partly destemmed, macerated for 30 days in steel and aged 18 months in concrete, at 14.5% alcohol, with ageing potential of over 15 years. It describes "a fine balance of elegance, generosity, velvetiness and finesse", with fine spices and stewed black fruit ([Bruno Lafon Selection](https://vincod.com/SQ8H1E/get/print)).

**The vintage.** 2016 is one of the great modern years in the southern Rhône. [Jancis Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jancis_Robinson)'s [vintage chart](https://www.jancisrobinson.com/learn/vintages/southern-rhone) quotes [Michel Chapoutier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chapoutier) saying it could be better than the legendary 1990. Warm conditions all year and reduced yields gave wines of great concentration in colour, tannin and flavour, "certainly one of the great vintages" for reds, and safe for cellaring into the 2030s.

**What the critics say for 2016.**
- I couldn't find a published critic's note for the 2016 Lucile Avril on pages I could read, so I've left critics out rather than guess.
- **[CellarTracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CellarTracker) community: 92.0** (from your CellarTracker list).

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is ten years old. Your CellarTracker list gives a window of 2020 to 2029, and the importer says over 15 years. From a great vintage and concrete-aged with no new oak, it should be in its prime: kirsch, black fruit, spice and garrigue. Decant an hour ahead.

**Serving and food.** The estate suggests 16°C and meats in sauce, such as [bœuf bourguignon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beef_bourguignon) or a Provençal [daube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daube), grilled meats and cheese ([Bruno Lafon Selection](https://vincod.com/SQ8H1E/get/print)).

**Value and where to buy.** None of the stores on this site lists Durieu at the moment.

**From the history books**
- **The popes and their castle.** In 1309 [Pope Clement V](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Clement_V) moved the papacy to [Avignon](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Palais+des+Papes,+Avignon,+France&t=k); his successor [John XXII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_John_XXII) built the summer castle that gave the village its name ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape_AOC)).
- **France's first appellation.** Local growers led by Baron [Pierre Le Roy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierre_Le_Roy_de_Boiseaumari%C3%A9) drew up France's first [appellation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appellation_d'origine_contr%C3%B4l%C3%A9e) rules in 1923, made law in 1936 ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape_AOC)).

**Curious details**
- **Five centuries in the village.** The Avril family arrived in Châteauneuf in the 1500s, so this cuvée carries a family name with nearly 500 years of local history ([Bruno Lafon Selection](https://vincod.com/SQ8H1E/get/print)).
- **The flying-cigar law.** In 1954, after local reports of [UFOs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flying_saucer), the Châteauneuf council banned "flying cigars" from flying over or landing in the commune ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape_AOC)).
